input.quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
input.rationale: Section 10(a) gives us a broad Vendor-side defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation covering third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient and its subcontractors. Because Kubient warrants at Section 9(b)(i) that the Service and deliverables do not infringe any third-party IP rights, and further warrants data security (9(b)(iii)) and compliance with applicable Law (9(b)(ix)), the indemnity reaches third-party IP infringement claims, Vendor-caused data breaches, breach of law and Vendor misconduct — the preferred position. Section 11 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice that is not a condition to recovery, indemnitor control of defence, no settlement admitting our liability without consent, cooperation at indemnitor's cost), and no sub-cap is imposed (Section 7(a) expressly carves indemnification out of the damages exclusion). The mirror Customer indemnity at 10(b) is directionally acceptable: it turns on our Content and Properties, our misuse and our own breach/acts. Its (v) "acts or omissions of Customer" limb is slightly wider than the playbook's ideal narrow scope, and the Creative limb of the Vendor indemnity is qualified by "to the best of its knowledge" — both are minor sub-elements noted here rather than redlined, since the clause as a whole meets the preferred position.
